runs.text:
The Millbrook Hollow City Council met Tuesday night. They voted to approve an amended parks and recreation line item. They talked about the Third Street bridge too. That replacement has been delayed a long time.

A spokesperson for the mayor's office said the new figure came from "ongoing conversations" among council members. She would not say what the conversations were. A memo from the finance subcommittee put the number at $340,000. A budget analyst looked at the memo. He said the number was in the range he expected.

Near the end of the memo there was a line about the bridge. No council member brought it up at the meeting. The lead structural engineer had found a crack in the load-bearing part. He said it was serious. He said the bridge should be closed to truck traffic within 90 days.

The bridge has been on the capital plan since 2019. It has had fourteen change orders. Nobody discussed it in detail.

After the meeting a reporter reached council member Dana Okafor. She said the process worked the way it was supposed to work. She said residents should feel good about that. She did not say anything else.
